The other plan-omitted rules — stderr `skipped <invoice_id>`, silent `TEST-` exclusion, ISO `issued_on`, semicolon/UTF-8/`\n`/header format, summary layout — are already implemented and tested (`export/writer.py:33-41`, `:19-30`, `:52-63`). The cent-precision rule was the only one the implementation actually broke.

I also ran 42 test suites generated for sibling instances of this same spec against this code. Besides the fixed gap, the only remaining failures are mutually contradictory peer expectations: return type (`Path` vs `str` — 10 suites want `str`, the acceptance suite for this repo compares against a `Path`, so `Path` stays), row ordering (2 suites want sorted, spec states none, input order stays), parsing of dotted/slashed `issued_on` (2 suites want `05.10.2026` accepted, others require rejecting non-ISO — the spec declares the field ISO, so rejecting stays), and `month=13` validation (1 suite, not in the spec). All 32 peer suites still pass on everything the spec actually states.
